chapter: Moving to New Orleans and country bands
title: What the country brass band played and Frankie Dusen teaching
summary: The brass band played marches and early jazz; Dusen taught them, though none may have read.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Well what kind of music did the brass band play? Did they play regular standard marches? Yeah. Hems or what?

They played marches, jazz numbers, I guess what they called you know at that time. They didn't understand, I don't guess they didn't understand much what they was doing anyway. But they wasn't up to like the fellas playing around here now, you know what I mean? Playing parades on the street. They had a band somewhere down on the other side of the river, I don't know who they was, from St. Sophie. They had a good band. They called him, you got a boy awake, they in the veteran hospital, call him Beam. Well he was really my cousin and he's Kent Sam. Sam was playing trumpet and he played trumpet. Well he had his band down there and Sam had his band up there around the ballet. But they, oh this fella was trying to figure, Frankie Doocy, that's the trombone player, was teaching them. Oh Doocy, Frankie?
That's the fella was teaching them. Wow.
That's a surprise. Was he much of a reader and all that, do you know? Doocy? Did he make any record?

Was he a reader? He was a good reader or what, do you know? Well I don't know, he was teaching them. Yeah, that's a surprise. And I never, I thought of him as a, mostly an ear man, I didn't know he was teaching them.
Well anyway, he was teaching them. And I don't tell you the facts, I don't know if any of them was reading at that time.
